footerTip.message: Tip: open chrome://discards to see the Auto Discardable column — tabs kept in memory show ✕. Note: manual discards there still work; this only blocks Chrome's automatic memory-saver discarding.

heroEyebrow.description: Small eyebrow text above the welcome title.

heroTitle.message: Keep the tabs that matter alive

heroLead.message: Chrome saves resources two ways: it unloads tabs you aren't using, and it slows down tabs you can't see. Keep Tabs Alive stops each — tab by tab, only where you want it.
heroLead.description: Intro paragraph on the welcome page.

wcard1Text.message: Chrome won't unload the tab, so its page state and ongoing work stay intact — no unexpected reloads. It may still slow down while hidden.

wcard2Text.message: The settings page lists every open tab with a Keep alive switch and two icons for Keep in memory and Keep running. They apply just to that tab.

wcard3Text.message: Protect everything except a few sites, or whitelist only the ones you choose. Rules match subdomains too — example.com covers all of it.
wcard3Text.description: Welcome card 3 body. Keep the <code> tag.

chooseYourSites.description: Primary call-to-action button on the welcome page.

actionsNote.message: Prefer to protect everything by default? You can switch modes in settings.

welcomeStep1.message: Pin it for one-click access: click the 🧩 puzzle icon in the toolbar, then the pin.
welcomeStep1.description: Welcome footer step 1. Keep the inline tags and the puzzle emoji.

tourMasterBody.message: Pause or resume Keep in memory for every tab here. While it's off, any tab may be unloaded — your rules are kept, just paused. Tabs you keep running stay running.

tourModeTitle.message: Which sites to keep in memory

tourModeBody.message: Only chosen sites keeps just the sites you list in memory (the gentle default). All sites, except… keeps every tab in memory except the sites you exclude. Keep running is set per tab, not here.
tourModeBody.description: Tour step body. Keep the <b> tags.

tourTabsBody.message: Every open tab has its own Keep in memory switch — a one-time choice that lasts until the tab is closed. The switch in a site's header does the same for the whole site, permanently. Click a row to jump to the tab.
tourTabsBody.description: Tour step body. Keep the <b> tags.

tourRulesBody.message: Add domains here to keep whole sites in memory (or to let Chrome unload them). A domain also covers its subdomains — example.com matches mail.example.com. That's the tour — reopen it any time from the ? button.
tourRulesBody.description: Tour step body. Keep the <code> tags.

tourBack.description: Tour: go to the previous step.

tourNext.description: Tour: go to the next step.

tourDone.description: Tour: finish on the last step.

runHelpTitle.description: Title of the explainer, tooltip of the ? button on the Keep running card.

runConsentTitle.message: Keep running simulates a screen recording

runHelpLead.message: Chrome slows down tabs you can't see. To prevent that, the extension simulates a screen recording of this tab, so Chrome treats it as in use.
runHelpLead.description: Explains why Keep running uses tab capture.

runHelpPoint1.message: Nothing is recorded. The picture is never read, saved or sent anywhere.

runHelpPoint2.message: Only this tab, and only while the switch is on. Chrome shows a sharing icon, so nothing happens in secret.

runHelpPoint3.message: Turn it off any time, or just close the tab.

consentCancel.description: Cancel button of the first-use dialog.

actionTitleRunning.message: Keep Tabs Alive — keeping tabs running
actionTitleRunning.description: Toolbar button tooltip while at least one tab is held by Keep running.

bannerText.message: Keep Tabs Alive is keeping this tab running

bannerHide.message: Hide this bar (the tab stays held)

timerForever.message: No timer — runs until you turn it off

memoryStop.message: Stop keeping this tab in memory

rowRunStart.message: Keep running — turn on for this tab

rowRunStop.message: Keep running is on — click to stop

tourRunBody.message: Need a page to keep working while hidden — a chat, a timer, live data? Open the popup on that tab and switch on Keep running, or press the bolt icon in the tab's row here. Chrome then treats the tab as in use, so it isn't slowed down. It simulates a screen recording — nothing is recorded or sent — and switches itself off after the timer you pick.

aliveTip.message: Keep this tab in memory and keep it running — both at once

runNeedsPopup.message: Chrome only allows this from the extension's window on that tab. Go to the tab and click the Keep Tabs Alive icon.

groupRunPick.message: Keep running works one tab at a time — pick a tab with its bolt button.

groupRunStartTip.message: Keep running: the page keeps working at full speed while hidden

groupRunStopTip.message: Stop Keep running for this site's tabs

aliveOnTabTip.message: Chrome allows Keep running only from the extension's window on that tab — this opens it there.

pendingBody.message: Close this window and click the Keep Tabs Alive icon (the green shield) in the toolbar — or under the puzzle-piece 🧩. Keep running turns on by itself.

handoffTitle.message: Turn on Keep running in the tab

handoffTitleAlive.message: Turn on Keep alive in the tab

handoffStep2.message: Click the blinking Keep Tabs Alive icon in the toolbar (the green shield). Don't see it? It's under the puzzle-piece 🧩.

handoffStep3.message: The window will point at the Keep running switch — click it, and it's on.

handoffStep3Alive.message: The window will point at the Keep running switch — click it, and the tab is kept in memory and running.

runDone.message: Done — this tab is kept running.

aliveDone.message: Done — this tab is kept alive: in memory and running.

memoryCardSub.message: Chrome won't unload these tabs — what you typed stays.

runCardSub.message: These pages keep working at full speed, even when hidden.

runEmpty.message: Nothing is kept running. Turn it on for a tab with ⚡ in the list below, or from the extension's window on that tab.

wMemDesc.message: Come back to it and everything is exactly where you left it — no reload.

wMemGain1.message: Typed text, drafts and forms stay

wMemCost.message: While hidden, the page may still slow down

wMemFor.message: long forms, documents, mail, dashboards you check now and then

wRunPromise.message: The page keeps working at full speed — even when you can't see it.

wRunDesc.message: Chrome treats the tab as in use, so nothing in it pauses while you're elsewhere.

wRunGain1.message: Chats, AI answers, timers, music and live data keep going

wRunGain2.message: Off by itself on a timer, if you like

wRunCost.message: Uses more battery; Chrome shows its screen-sharing icon — nothing is recorded

wRunFor.message: chats and AI tools, trading and monitoring, timers, uploads

wBoth.message: Need both? “Keep alive” turns on both modes for a tab in one click.

wStep2.message: On any tab, click the icon — its window has a switch for each mode.

wStep3.message: In Settings see every open tab, and keep whole sites in memory.

wPrivacy.message: Nothing leaves your browser: no tracking, no servers. Keep running never records the page.
